_comment: PERMANENT runtime statement for IAM user mcaffeine-erp-prefg-tool in account
That user carries several separate policies: the deploy one in
deploy/iam-policy-erp-app-deploy.json (ECR, SSM, EC2, CloudWatch), an S3 one
not currently in this repo, and this. Attaching this as its own policy keeps
This is the entire runtime cost of the SES migration: one statement, no new
secret. That is why SES was chosen over Resend/Postmark.
SECURITY NOTE - the same user's keys serve both the running app and the
deploy tooling, so those keys already grant ssm:SendCommand with
AWS-RunShellScript on the two app instances plus read/write on all
/erp-app/* secrets. That concentration predates this migration and is out of
its scope, but it is the reason the ses:FromAddress condition below must
stay: the blast radius of these credentials is already wide.

_comment_condition: DO NOT REMOVE THE CONDITION. The identity is the ROOT domain
mcaffeine.com, so without it this credential can send as ANY address at
mcaffeine.com - ceo@, accounts@, anyone. The condition is the only thing
between a leaked app key and company-wide impersonation. With a subdomain
identity it would be good practice; with a root-domain identity it is the
primary control.
BOTH identity ARNs are listed on purpose. Probed 2026-08-05: SES
authorised SendEmail against the ADDRESS-level ARN
identity/erp.prefg@mcaffeine.com
not the domain-level one. It may switch to the domain ARN once
mcaffeine.com is verified as a domain identity - the behaviour was not
determinable before that existed. Listing both covers either case and
widens nothing, because ses:FromAddress below is what actually restricts
the sender. Do not 'tidy up' by removing one.
The configuration set ARN is also required, because lib/mailer.ts passes
ses.ConfigurationSetName on every send. Omit it and every send fails with
AccessDenied.
BOTH ses:SendEmail AND ses:SendRawEmail are required. Verified the hard
way on 2026-08-19: with only ses:SendEmail, a real send through the app
failed with
AccessDenied: not authorized to perform 'ses:SendRawEmail'
The IAM action depends on the CONTENT TYPE, not the API version. The
nodemailer SES transport sends Content.Raw.Data, and IAM authorises raw
content as ses:SendRawEmail even though the call is the SESv2
SendEmailCommand. ses:SendEmail alone covers only Simple/Templated
content - which is why an `aws sesv2 send-email --content Simple={...}`
probe passes while the application fails. Do not 'simplify' this back to
one action on the basis of the v1/v2 distinction; that reasoning is wrong.
If a second sender is ever added (a different address or another app),
give it its own statement with its own FromAddress rather than widening
this one to a list.
